name: Mandatory and task training
summary: Ontario law requires every new underground miner to complete the four common core modules before working, and every worker to hold the specialty modules and equipment training for each task. Two site trainers run the common core classes and refreshers, while task training on machines happens on production shifts with an experienced operator coaching and the trainer signing off. The HSE manager, as the site's designated signing authority, approves accreditations, and the trainer keeps the records that supervisors check at line-up. The process is slow because trainees, machines and coaches must be released from production on a 14-on/14-off rotation, and training is the first thing cut when crews are short.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian gold producer running a 500-650 tpd underground mine and its own mill near Wawa in northern Ontario, with 12-hour shifts on 14-on/14-off rotations and a camp.
baseline.notes: About 10 new hires a month and a site roster of about 380 people including contractors, who are trained by their own employers.

unit_of_work: one training course (a common core class, a task training sign-off on one machine, or a refresher class)
trigger: HR sends a new-hire list, a supervisor asks for task training, a refresher falls due, or a safety alert needs to be taught.
end_state: The trainees are assessed competent, the records are signed and entered, and supervisors know the workers can be assigned.

volume.seasonality: Busier in January-March (refresher cycle and new budget hiring) and when expansion hiring brings larger new-hire groups.

evidence.note: Kept from the organisation file.

surge.cause: Hiring wave for a production ramp-up or a contractor-to-owner conversion

evidence.note: Author's estimate; production rose from 2019 to 2020 at the modelled mine (organisation file).
Both trainers spend their time on this process.
Stands in for trainees of all trades: class and practical time of workers in training, about 40 hours a year for each of about 300 employees plus common core for new hires.
Trainee and experienced coach time on task training shifts.
Releasing trainees and machines.
Signing authority approvals.

systems.name: Incident, inspection and training records system
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)
Shift reports, line-up boards and production tallies (paper and spreadsheets)
Leaky feeder radio and surface radio network

resources.name: Training room at the mine dry
Underground utility fleet (scissor lifts and light vehicles)

steps.name: Receive the training request and check the matrix
steps.description: The trainer gets a request: a new-hire list from HR, a supervisor asking for a worker to be trained on a machine, an expiring refresher flagged in the training records system, or a safety alert that needs a talk. They check the training matrix for which modules each worker already holds and which are required for the job.

error.defect_description: A required module or an expired ticket is missed because the matrix is out of date.

evidence.note: Employers must train workers in the common core and specialty modules Regulation 854 requires and on their specific equipment; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Schedule the course around the rotation
steps.description: The trainer finds dates when the trainees, a trainer and the training room or machine are all available, which on a 14-on/14-off rotation usually means the start of the trainees' next hitch, and asks the supervisors to release the workers from the line-up.

next.condition: task or specialty module on equipment
trainees pulled back to production: rebook

evidence.note: Mix of course types and rebooking share are the author's estimates: about ten new hires a month (organisation file, site-recruitment) in groups of three, most other courses being task training and refreshers.

steps.name: Teach the common core classroom modules
steps.description: The trainer delivers the surface and underground induction and the theory of the general inspection, scaling and lockout modules in the training room, with videos, the site's procedures and written checks.

control.basis: Regulation 854 s. 11: basic common core program (Underground Hard Rock Miner 770010) completed before the work is assigned

evidence.note: The four common core modules (U0000 induction, U0001 inspections, U0002 scaling, U0012 lockout) are named on the review page; classroom length is the author's estimate.

steps.name: New hires attend the classroom modules
steps.description: A group of new miners sits the classroom part of the common core, reading the procedures and completing the written checks for each module. They are paid but not on the line-up.

evidence.note: Group of three is the author's estimate; dev-miner stands in for new underground hires of all trades.

steps.name: Coach the underground practical modules
steps.description: The trainer takes the group underground to practise workplace inspection, scaling with a bar and lockout on a real machine, and observes each person doing each task to the module's performance standard.

control.basis: Regulation 854 s. 11 and the program guideline: competency in each common core module demonstrated before accreditation

evidence.note: Competency demonstration and accreditation by the signing authority are described on the review page; hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: New hires practise underground under supervision
steps.description: The new miners scale loose rock, inspect their workplace and lock out a machine under the trainer's eye, repeating each task until it meets the module's performance standard.

evidence.note: Runs alongside s05.

steps.name: Release a trainee and a machine for task training
steps.description: The shift supervisor picks a shift when a machine (a scooptram, bolter or jumbo) and an experienced operator can be spared from production, and puts the trainee with them on the line-up.
outputs: trainee lined up with coach and machine

evidence.note: Machines and coaches are released only when production allows; wait is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Trainer instructs and checks the trainee on the machine
steps.description: The trainer gives the pre-operation instruction on the machine (walk-around, controls, emergency stops, the site's traffic rules), comes back at the end of the coaching shifts, and watches the trainee operate before the sign-off.
inputs: trainee lined up with coach and machine

control.basis: Regulation 854 s. 11: specialty modules required for the task completed by the worker

evidence.note: Specialty modules (75 in the underground program) are taken as required under s. 11; hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Trainee operates beside an experienced operator
steps.description: Over one to three shifts the trainee runs the machine with an experienced operator beside them, who coaches and corrects; production from the heading is lower while this happens.

evidence.note: Two people (trainee and coach) for one to three 10-hour working shifts is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Rebook trainees pulled back to production
steps.description: When a supervisor keeps the trainees on the line-up because of absences or a production push, the trainer cancels the booking and looks for the next slot, usually on the following rotation.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the refresher or safety talk
steps.description: The trainer updates the slides and test for the refresher (WHMIS, lockout, ground control awareness, a recent safety alert), prints the attendance sheet and books the training room.

evidence.note: Author's estimate. The review page notes there was no formal refresher requirement, so refreshers follow the company program.

steps.name: Deliver the refresher class
steps.description: The trainer runs the class in the training room, works through the site examples and recent incidents, takes questions, gives the short written test and collects the signed attendance sheets.

control.basis: Company refresher training program (no provincial refresher requirement for mining modules in 2019-2022)

evidence.note: Absence of a formal refresher requirement from the review page; class length is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Workers attend the refresher
steps.description: A group of miners, mill or maintenance workers sits the class at the start of their shift or hitch and writes the test.

evidence.note: Class of eight is the author's estimate; dev-miner stands in for site workers of all trades.

steps.name: Assess competency and sign the module records
steps.description: The trainer marks the tests, completes the module performance checklists and signs each trainee's record; a trainee who does not meet the standard is booked for more practice.

error.defect_description: Checklist signed with a task not actually observed.

control.basis: Ontario modular training program guidelines: competency in each module assessed and recorded before accreditation

evidence.note: Competency determination for accreditation from the review page; pass share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Book remedial practice
steps.description: The trainer tells the supervisor what the trainee still needs to practise and books another session, usually on the next shifts the trainee works.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Signing authority approves the accreditation
steps.description: The site's designated signing authority, the HSE manager, reviews the signed module records and signs off the accreditation for common core and specialty modules; for refreshers this is a check of the attendance sheet.

control.basis: Designated signing authority under the Ontario modular training program, accountable for training quality, records and competency decisions

evidence.note: Role of the designated signing authority from the review page; the HSE manager holding it and the review time are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Enter the training records
steps.description: The trainer types each completion into the training records system with dates and module numbers, scans the signed forms to the employee's file, and sends common core and specialty module completions to the provincial training registry.

error.defect_description: Wrong module number or date typed, so the record shows a gap later.

control.basis: Ontario modular training program: training records kept by the designated signing authority

evidence.note: Record keeping by the signing authority from the review page; the provincial registry submission and minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Tell supervisors the workers are cleared
steps.description: The trainer emails the supervisors and updates the training board in the line-up room so the workers can be assigned to the new task or machine from their next shift.

evidence.note: Supervisors check training before lining workers up (organisation file process description); minutes are the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Trainees pulled back to production
exceptions.description: A supervisor short of crew keeps the trainees on the line-up and the course moves to the next rotation.

exceptions.name: Not yet competent
exceptions.description: The trainee needs more practice and is booked for another session before sign-off.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from training request to workers cleared
benchmarks.population: Training courses at an Ontario underground mine on a 14/14 rotation

evidence.note: Most courses wait for the trainees' next hitch (up to 14 days) and a free machine, then a few days for sign-off and records.

benchmarks.unit: mandatory modules (Underground Hard Rock Miner program 770010)

pain_points.description: Trainees, coaches and machines are released only when production allows, so task training slips from rotation to rotation and limits who can be lined up.

evidence.note: Organisation file process description and author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Paper checklists are signed, scanned and re-typed into the training records system, and the line-up board is updated by hand.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of 2019-2022 practice.

pain_points.description: Approvals wait for the signing authority's days on site.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

sources.title: Mining health, safety and prevention review final report: training, skills and labour supply
sources.publisher: Government of Ontario (archived copy in the Library and Archives Canada web archive)
sources.supports: Employers train workers in the common core and specialty modules required by Regulation 854 (specialty modules under s. 11) and on the specific equipment they use; the Underground Hard Rock Miner program 770010 has four mandatory common core modules (U0000 induction, U0001 general inspections, U0002 scaling, U0012 lockout and tagging) and 75 specialty modules taken as required; each employer has a designated signing authority accountable for training quality, records and competency decisions; no formal refresher requirement; supervisors can start before completing supervisory common core. Page dated 1 March 2022, capture of 4 December 2022.

assumptions: One case is one course. Common core classes are about 13% of courses (about four classes of three new hires a month), task training sign-offs about 52% and refresher classes about 28%.

Trainees of all trades are entered as dev-miner (and lhd-operator for task training) because the organisation file has no generic trainee role; their fte_on_process is time in training, not a headcount.

The organisation file lists only site-recruitment as a trigger; most courses are requested by supervisors when the line-up check finds a missing or expiring module, so mine-shift-control, mill-grind-leach and mnt-work-planning were added as triggers. Safety alerts are treated as a trigger for refresher talks rather than a standing input.
The scooptram held during task training (s08, s09) still does some production work, so the resource cost per case overstates the lost machine time.

The simulated median of about 17 days is above the 12-day estimate mainly because of the wait for the trainees' next rotation (s02) and for the signing authority (s16); both waits are kept because rotation scheduling is the main constraint the organisation file describes.
The HSE manager is assumed to be the site's designated signing authority.
Common core length (two to three classroom shifts and one underground shift) is the author's estimate; the program page opened does not state hours.
The trainers have no shift pattern in the organisation file (office hours); a rotation pattern would shorten s02 waits slightly.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's rates: base wage times 1.30 for office and staff roles and 1.35 for hourly site roles.
